paragraphs.text: Coral reefs damaged by storms and warming seas can take decades to recover naturally. To speed this up, marine biologists in several countries are growing corals in underwater nurseries.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: Small fragments are cut from healthy corals and attached to frames shaped like trees, which hang in the water a few metres below the surface. Here the fragments receive plenty of light and are kept away from the sea floor, where sand can bury them.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: After six to twelve months, the fragments have grown large enough to be moved. Divers attach them to damaged parts of the reef using a special underwater glue or small metal nails.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Scientists try to use corals that survived recent heatwaves, in the hope that these will cope better with future rises in temperature.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Volunteers from local diving clubs often help with this work, and some projects allow tourists to join a dive to see the nurseries for themselves.
paragraphs.label: E
